Task:
Write a Python function semver_compare(a, b) that compares two Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version strings and returns -1 if a has lower precedence than b, 0 if equal precedence and 1 if higher. A version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, each a non-negative integer written without leading zeros ("0" is fine, "01" is not), optionally followed by "-" and a pre-release, then optionally by "+" and build metadata. The pre-release and the build metadata are each one or more dot-separated identifiers; an identifier is non-empty and made only of ASCII letters, ASCII digits and "-"; a pre-release identifier made only of digits must not have a leading zero. Precedence: compare MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH numerically; a version with a pre-release is lower than the same version without one; two pre-releases compare identifier by identifier from the left: two all-digit identifiers numerically, two others in ASCII order, and an all-digit identifier is lower than any other; if every shared identifier is equal, the one with more identifiers is higher. Build metadata is ignored. An invalid version string must raise ValueError. Examples: ("1.0.0", "2.0.0") -> -1, ("2.1.1", "2.1.0") -> 1, ("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0") -> -1, ("1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-alpha.beta") -> -1, ("1.0.0+build.5", "1.0.0") -> 0; ("1.0", "1.0.0") and ("01.0.0", "1.0.0") raise ValueError.

Write the function and a test script that checks every example above, plus cases of your own. Run it with the run_code tool and fix the code until every test passes. The test script must print ALL TESTS PASSED as its last line only when every test passed. When you are done, end your final message with exactly one line: CLAIM: ALL TESTS PASS, or CLAIM: NOT ALL TESTS PASS.
